samples.identity: Fixed VHD, NTFS volume, order-lure batch downloader
evidence: Allocated Order0324fpubh-10-994125-1.bat launches minimized PowerShell with WindowStyle Hidden. It builds the function: provider, registers a stride-two character decoder and a wrapper that dot-invokes decoded IEX.

Decoder takes indices 1,3,5,... . Decoded commands construct System.Net.WebClient, select TLS 1.2, set a Firefox User-Agent, and DownloadFile https://www.chirreeirl.com/wp-panel/uploads/Slippy.dwp to AppData/Emsige.Vis. The retry loop sleeps four seconds and checks Test-Path.

Reads downloaded data, FromBase64String, ASCII.GetString, Substring(433151,27691), then passes the result through the IEX wrapper. Batch %% expansion must precede stride decoding. Final payload could not be retrieved: forager returned NXDOMAIN.

Base64 UTF-16LE script residue at offsets 0x57a61, 0x2e2f42, 0x306694 and 0x522795 reconstructs AmsiInitialize and GetProcAddress through byte arrays, builds native delegates, walks 32/64-bit provider vtables, changes protection, copies B8 00 00 00 00 C3 over scan routines, verifies bytes, and restores protection. Its -DisableSvc path reconstructs EtwEventWrite and writes RET on x64 (different three-byte x86 patch). Top-level invocation specifies -DisableSvc. Residue is not an allocated launchable member and is not claimed to execute with the batch.
No legitimate order-processing purpose explains hidden downloaded evaluation and security-control patching. Payload identity and deployment context remain unknown.
samples.coverage: Two new suspicious findings in allocated batch: concealed stride reconstruction and hidden-window downloader. Two further suspicious security-patch findings match the manually recovered script and a standalone Base64/UTF-16LE representation. No unsupported final-payload identity or success claim.
samples.engine_gap: Installed atomscan 2.13.0 treats VHD as unknown and misses members. Current source-matched Cleave recognizes VHD and extracts batch. Neither archive analysis nor encoded test-match exposes unallocated Base64 script as a decoded analysis unit; its patch findings require forensic extraction.

samples.identity: Rifaien v1.0 self-submission client, UPX-packed Win32 console executable
evidence: UPX checksum mismatch blocks normal unpacking. Emulated decompression/branch repair recovers OEP 0x401130, CRT 0x401020 and main 0x4013a0. Constructor table at 0x41de20 is ffffffff,00000000: no application constructors. Import restoration and final jump in UPX stub are ordinary loader mechanics.

Main gets its own module filename (0x4013ce), reads entire file and searches [[UNIQUE]] (0x401470). Every 30 seconds it chooses NODE1 through NODE7, creates a random 16-character filename, mutates 16 bytes after the slot, writes a full self-copy, and libcurl-posts fields file[], node, submit to the fixed /upload endpoint; it unlinks submitted copies. No response-to-execution path or arbitrary host-file source was found.

Overlay begins at 0x14c8b, contains native XOR string decoding, CLR-host GUIDs and resource-loading/managed invocation code. It is truncated: resource raw offset 0x22000 is beyond the 123389 available overlay bytes. Outer loader, empty constructor table and main neither map nor invoke it. These are accurate static capabilities/structure in embedded data and are retained.

Fetched exact Triage report plus behavioral1/static1: observed one application process and periodic POSTs of approximately this sample size to /upload, receiving HTTP 301. This corroborates the recovered client path; Snojan attribution/score is not behavior evidence.

Forager attempts to fetch HTTP and HTTPS endpoint failed (timeout and broken TLS certificate). Historical public-VM context is corroborative only; current endpoint ownership and actual deployment authorization are unknown. No hostile dependency, persistence, downloaded execution or host-data theft established.
samples.why_external_label: Inference: UPX checksum failure, mutation, repeated self-copy/submission, suspicious endpoint reputation, and inert embedded protected-code fragments can produce worm/downloader signatures. Triage labels Snojan but its observed requests are uploads, consistent with this client.

samples.identity: eBay Security Center Advisory HTML phishing email
evidence: Uses real eBay logo/click resources and 2004 copyright to impersonate an account-security notice. Claims random security maintenance and threatens account suspension.

The account-verification call to action links http://196.32.0.12/asp/ebayDLLupdate/index.html instead of an eBay origin. It is a navigation lure; there is no inline form, JavaScript, obfuscation, local credential collection or demonstrated submission in this artifact.

Brand impersonation, coercion and offsite verification destination establish phishing without assuming a successful downstream credential capture. Historical landing-page availability and actual delivery are unknown.
